title: Edge continuity: graceful weighted shifts with stream-aware circuit breakers
creator: Aisha Raman
body:
Summary:
We need a production-safe approach for active-active edge/gateway failover that preserves streaming session continuity where possible, enforces SLOs, and protects downstream capacity with circuit breakers and progressive load shedding. This ticket defines the design, rollout plan, telemetry, and validation tests for a weighted graceful traffic shift paired with stream-aware circuit breaker logic.

Goals:
- Maintain p99 tail latency SLOs for hosted API endpoints during region-level degradation and cross-region shifts.
- Avoid mid-stream abrupt disconnects for long-lived streaming sessions where possible (reduce user-perceived interruptions).
- Protect model-serving clusters from sudden overload by tripping circuit breakers early and enabling policy-driven load shedding.
- Provide clear observability (per-session, per-region, per-model) and automated rollback triggers tied to error budget burn.

Non-goals:
- This is not a redesign of session token formats. We accept existing session IDs and stream tokens as the affinity keys.
- We will not change upstream billing or quota semantics in this iteration.

Design overview:
1) Weighted graceful shift: when region A degrades, the gateway manager initiates a windowed weighted shift to region B. Traffic weights move in small increments (default 5% per 30s) with a configurable stabilization period at each step. The shift controller respects route-level policies (model compatibility, customer pref) and excludes endpoints with session affinity if the policy requires sticky handling.

2) Stream-aware affinity & handover: for streaming sessions identified by session_id or stream_token, the gateway will attempt soft-handover before shifting traffic away:
   - If a session is active and client supports resume tokens, gateway routes existing frames to the original region until session completes or maximum handover timeout (default 90s) is reached.
   - If resume not supported or timeout reached, gateway will failover new frames to the failover region and attach a short-lived handoff header to help the model service reconcile partial state.

3) Circuit breakers and progressive load-shedding:
   - Per-backend circuit breakers evaluate request queue growth, CPU/GPU saturation, and tail latency. If any breach threshold sustained for N samples, breaker opens for that backend and gateway reroutes new requests according to policy (fallback model variant, alternate region, or return 503 with retry-after).
   - Load shedding tiers: Tier 1 (non-critical low-cost paths) shed first; Tier 2 (non-interactive/bulk jobs) shed next; Tier 3 (interactive/chat completions) protected longest. Policies configurable by customer tier.

4) SLO & error-budget integration:
   - Define SLOs per-route/model for availability and p99 latency. The shift controller consults remaining error budget before advancing weights; if error budget burn is high, shifts slow down or abort and an alert page is raised.

5) Observability & automations:
   - New dashboards: per-region session continuity rate, handover-time histogram, circuit-breaker open rate, weight-change timeline.
   - Automated rollback trigger: if p99 increases >25% over baseline for 3 consecutive windows or circuit-breaker open rate exceeds 15% for 5m, automated rollback to last-known-good distribution.

Data flows and compatibility notes:
- Only compatible model variants (same tokenizer/architecture) are eligible for automatic fallback. Incompatible fallbacks must be explicitly declared in model catalog.
- For VPC/private deployments, default remote region shift is disabled unless customer enables cross-region failover.

Operational runbook (high-level):
- Detect: telemetry (region error rate, queue length) triggers alarm.
- Respond: shift controller begins weighted shift; notify on-call; create incident with proposed weight plan.
- Mitigate: if circuit breaker trips, block additional traffic and route to fallbacks or reject as configured.
- Recover: after stabilization, gradually restore normal weights and mark incident resolved.

Testing & validation plan:
- Unit/Integration: simulate weight transitions with synthetic sessions (short and long lived) and assert continuity rates.
- Load tests: inject region-level latency and capacity limits, validate circuit breaker trips at expected thresholds and that load-shedding prioritization matches policy.
- Chaos tests: blackout a region in staging, run long-running streams to verify resume behaviour and handover timeouts.
- User acceptance: run a canary with 5% of production traffic routed through new controller for 48h.

Acceptance criteria:
- Must maintain <=10% increase in p99 latency during successful graceful shift in staging under modeled load.
- Session continuity (no forced reconnect) for >=95% of resumable streams during a 5% canary shift.
- Circuit breakers trigger within defined thresholds and downstream services do not exceed 85% GPU utilization.
- Dashboards and alerts present in Console; runbook published and linked in incident templates.

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/edge-resilience/design (prototype plan and sequence diagrams)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4832 (shift controller state machine)
- Telemetry dashboard draft: https://app.console/redwood/dashboards/edge-shift-proto

Follow-ups and open decisions:
- Decide default weight step and stabilization windows per route complexity (latency-sensitive vs batch).
- Define exact headers and reconcile with model-onboarding for handoff metadata.
- Evaluate cost implications for cross-region sustained shifts and quotas.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: long-lived streams prolong recovery and complicate capacity planning. Mitigation: handover timeout and explicit session termination policies for high-impact incidents.
- Risk: Too-aggressive automatic shifts could worsen error budget burn. Mitigation: guardrails via SLO-aware controls and manual override.

Next steps:
1) Exec review of design doc (owner: Aisha) -> due 2026-03-09.
2) Implementation sprints: controller + circuit-breaker metrics (owner: Diego) -> land core in runtime-2.2.
3) Staging chaos + canary -> 2-week validation window.
